# MOL import atropisomer regressions

The `geometry-*.mol` and `rings-*.mol` files are generated by the existing
`reference/atropisomer_reference.py` cases, using RDKit 2026.03.6. They cover
#1057 and the named counterexamples in #1053/#1059; geometry/1160 also pins
#1065's existing MOL behavior.

| Fixture | Reference case |
| --- | --- |
| geometry-824.mol | geometry/824 |
| geometry-1160.mol | geometry/1160 |
| geometry-1506.mol | geometry/1506 |
| geometry-3583.mol | geometry/3583 |
| geometry-4110.mol | geometry/4110 |
| geometry-4327.mol | geometry/4327 |
| rings-biaryl-31.mol | rings/Fc1cccc(F)c1-c1c(Cl)cccc1Cl/False/31 |
| rings-pyrrole-17.mol | rings/c1ccccc1-n1cccc1/True/17 |
| rings-amide-21.mol | rings/O=C(Nc1ccccc1)c1ccccc1/False/21 |
| rings-stilbene-34.mol | rings/c1ccccc1/C=C/c1ccccc1/False/34 |

`binol-2d.mol` is the existing `binol_mol(1)` input from
`crates/io/src/chemistry/axial_tests.rs`, whose drawn wedge keeps the P axis.
The tests reuse the existing axis-free 3D alkane fixtures from
`tests/fixtures/mol-import-3d`.

`binol-2d-explicit-h.mol` adds an ordinary terminal hydrogen as the first
atom of that BINOL input; folding it leaves stable atom IDs with a gap.
